March 27th 2025 From Patty Barber Hiram Maine I am writing in support of LD 348 Resolve to Study the Effects of High Intensity Headlights on Drivers
Thank you to the sponsors for spearheading this bill!! This addresses such a serious safety and health issue-the new headlights are severely blinding -both for oncoming cars and for cars following you while driving at night.
I find that I have to look away from oncoming cars as they approach me. That cannot be a safe way to drive! It then takes a few minutes before my vision readjusts to be able to see the road again, that is until the next car approaches.
A similar situation occurs when a car is behind me. The headlights cause such a glare in both the rearview and the side mirrors that I am constantly trying to adjust my mirrors to minimize the reflection. This certainly takes away from my focus on the road ahead.
It has become so bad, that I dread to drive at night, which is a near impossible task to avoid when one has to commute in Maine in the dark fall and winter seasons.
Incandescent lights both for home and vehicles have been banned from the US under a misguided notion that LED lights are better for people and energy use. I have found this to be problematic.
Personally I have found that LED lights in the home are detrimental to my vision and cause me headaches. The glare is uncomfortable, even for the so called 'warmer' versions. The fact that I can't just go to the store and buy incandescent bulbs to be able to maximize my comfort and health is discerning. I'm not sure who decided incandescent bulbs should be outlawed, but whoever that was took away my ability to choose what works best for me.
I assume we are dealing with the same issue with headlights, that they are now mandated to all be LEDs. Or perhaps there are other reasons the current headlights are so intrusive and detrimental to our vision and our ability to drive safety.
This study will answer many of those questions, and hopefully outline fixes that alleviate the problems. Please support this initiative to study these headlights. (And support the return of incandescent light bulbs to Maine!)
Patty Barber

DONE: RE: LD 348 March 28, 2025
The recent proliferation of high-intensity bluish white headlights on vehicles, especially trucks, had
made it very difficult, if not dangerous, for me to drive at night. And I am not alone. The brilliant brightness not only hurts my eyes, but creates such a radiant glare that it obliterates the view of not only the other lane, but also my driving lane and beyond. There is no way I would be able to see another
vehicle, judge the distance or even see an animal or person near or in the road. Having cataracts and
being blinded by the bright blue-white high beams creates this hazardous driving situation. Many folks
are unable to have corrective surgery, yet continue to drive at night out of neccessity. Once corrective surgery is done, the bright lights still hurt the eyes, but visibility has improved. Not everyone can afford or are willing to have the surgery. Please consider studying the use of these blue-white brights. Let's go
back to the just the warm lights we have always successfully used. Thank you.

Department of the Secretary of State Bureau of Motor Vehicles
Shenna Bellows Catherine Curtis Secretary of State Deputy Secretary of State
JOmT STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORTATION
L.D. 348 "An Act to Study the Effect of High-intensity Headlights on Drivers."
Testimony of Sheima Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State March 28, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation, I am providing testimony Neither for Nor Against L.D. 348 "An Act to Study the Effect of High-intensity Headlights on Drivers." The Bureau of Motor Vehicles supports roadway safety by ensuring drivers possess the knowledge, skills and driving history to operate safely and that vehicles meet qualification to be registered and titled.
This bill requires the Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles to convene and staff a group to study the effects ofhigh-intensity headlights on drivers and to report back to this committee its findings and recommendations. There are Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS) that regulate headlights that are installed in vehicles by manufacturers. However, there are also after-market products such as headlights, available to consumers which are not regulated by these federal standards. It is our understanding that some of these headlights are affecting other drivers when meeting vehicles head-on at night. While we are committed to supporting roadway safety and we understand the concerns this study is trying to address, our bureau does not regulate vehicle parts or the sale of vehicle parts, nor do we have the expertise to address or solve this problem. We do not oppose this, but we do not believe the Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Motor Vehicles is the appropriate agency to lead this effort. The safety of Maine's road users is of paramount importance to the Department, and it is for these reasons we ask that if you approve this bill, another entity with more expertise in this area is directed to convene and staff the effort. Thank you for your time today and I will be happy to answer any questions.
